summary: Giulia Porru worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a Ph.D. at the University of Florence under Giacomo Devoto (~1933–1937). She became Professore incaricato di filologia Germanica at the University of Florence in 1946.
Giuliana Martini is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University in 2010.

Giuliana Stramiglioni was a Japanologist who studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1932–1936). She held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (1938), taught Italian at the University of Tokyo (until 1965), and was Professor of Japanese at Sapienza University of Rome (1965–1985).

Giuseppe Bardelli was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He held posts at the University of Pisa (1843, 1849–1851, 1862), Laurentian Library (1852), and Istituto di Studi Superiori di Firenze (1859–1862).

Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti was a linguist who held posts at the University of Bologna as professor of Hebrew (1797), professor (1804–1808), and professor of Oriental languages and Ancient Greek (~1803–1831). He became Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library in 1833.

Giuseppe De Lorenzo studied at the University of Naples Federico II (~1888–1893) and under Karl Eugen Neumann. He worked in Buddhist studies, serving as PD (1897) and Professor of Geology and Physical Geography (1905–1941) at the University of Naples Federico II.
Giuseppe Maria da Gargnano was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Sapienza University of Rome and served as vice-prefect of the Tibet Mission in 1758.
Giuseppe Mezzofanti studied at the University of Bologna (~1793–1799) and held a post there from ~1797 to 1831.

Giuseppe Toscano was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore (1938–1942) and served as director of the Museo d'Arte Cinese ed Etnografico (~1965–1988).

Giuseppe Tucci studied at Sapienza University under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca. A scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and history/archaeology, he held posts at Visva-Bharati, Dhaka, Calcutta, Naples, Sapienza (1932–1969), and directed Serie Orientale Roma (~1950–1978).

Giuseppe Turrini was an Indologist who studied at the University of Padua and the University of Pisa under Giuseppe Bardelli and Gaspare Gorresio. In 1860, he became Professore ordinario di filologia indo-europea at the University of Bologna.

Giuseppe Vignato works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Peking University under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, and held an attested post there in 2017.

Giuseppina Scalabrino Borsani was an Indologist who studied at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore under Ambrogio Ballini (~1929–1933). She later served as an assistant at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore from 1954 to 1980.

Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1926) and Toyo University (professor, 1927).

Glenn H. Mullin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Ling Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama, and founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and the traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Glyn Richards worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, studying at the University of Wales, Oxford, and McMaster. He held posts at McMaster (1968–1970), Carleton (1970–1973), and the University of Stirling (1973–1990), where he was Head of Religious Studies.
Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Godabarish Mishra studied at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta in philosophy and economics. Active in Indology and philosophy, he taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and served as Director at the University of Madras.

Godamune Chullanaga is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the Indian Cultural Centre, Sri Jinarathana Vocational Training Center, the University of Kelaniya, and the Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka.
